cues: Opens with "I have the method guidance... principles and procedures detailed in the plan framework. I'll work through all 10 steps in order," which refers directly to a written methodology.

Fixed, numbered section structure (Classification and Constraints, Dependencies, Key decisions, First end-to-end slice, Phases, Validation checks, Cross-Cutting Concerns, AI Layer, Exceptions, Deferred). This looks like a template, not free-form planning.
Jargon that only makes sense inside a framework: reversibility tags R1/R2/R3, gate IDs V0/V1/V1b/V2/V3, "Phase 0 first end-to-end slice," and "Principle 7 — first after skeleton."
Validation gates each have fixed fields (hypothesis, method, acceptance threshold, evidence, unlocks, phase). Decision rows have fixed fields too (default, assumption, validated by, revisit trigger).

Ends with a "Self-Check" that ticks off framework rules ("Rework runs widest first," "Exposure runs smallest first," "Each R3 row cites a V-ID"). It also has explicit N/A lines, a "Nothing the request does not need" check, and "Exceptions" and "Deferred" sections with pull-forward conditions.
